audited_plan.image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on blue water. The bird is in a standard upright swimming posture, not preening. It displays the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, and brownish-grey body. The bill is clearly visible, showing a yellow-green color with a dark tip. The eye is dark and distinct. The water surface shows ripples and a reflection of the bird's head and neck.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is fully visible and exposed in a standard floating pose. It exhibits the correct broad, flat shape and the expected yellow-green coloration with a darker tip, matching the taxonomy description.
The eye is clearly visible on the side of the head. It appears as a distinct dark spot against the iridescent green feathers, consistent with the 'dark eyes' checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a drake, appearing buoyant and streamlined on the water surface. The plumage texture looks dense and waterproof, sitting correctly on the water line.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the diagnostic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brown/grey body plumage. This matches the specific breeding plumage description provided.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged underwater and not visible in the image. This is a genuine occlusion case for a floating bird.

The folded wings are visible on the side of the body, showing the correct placement and general shape consistent with a swimming duck. While 'pointed' is hard to judge when folded, the broad structure is evident.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail area is visible at the rear of the bird. The short tail structure is present, and there is a hint of the characteristic curl (drake feather) at the very end, though subtle due to the angle.
